groups.title: Rendering Mental Models
groups.question: Your product page reads from the database, has an add-to-cart button and slow reviews. Explain where each part renders and how the page can show content before everything loads.

followUps.Server vs client component boundary rule: What decides whether a component runs on the server or in the browser?
followUps.Static vs dynamic rendering strategies: What makes a route dynamic instead of static?
followUps.Streaming and progressive page hydration: How does streaming let users see content before slow data arrives?

evidence.text: Server components run only on the server and can access the database directly.
Client components run in the browser and handle interactivity and state.
The use client directive marks where the client part of the tree starts.

notEnough: Only saying there are two kinds of components.

evidence.text: Routes are rendered statically at build time by default.
Using request data like cookies or headers makes the route render per request.
Static is faster and cacheable; dynamic gives fresh, per-user content.

notEnough: Only saying routes can be static or dynamic.

evidence.text: The server sends HTML in chunks as it becomes ready.
Slow components wrapped in Suspense show a fallback first.
Users see and use the rest of the page sooner.

groups.title: Caching and Revalidation Theory
groups.question: After editing a product, users still see the old price for a while. Explain how Next.js caches data and how you would refresh it.

followUps.Next.js caching layers and how they inte: What are Next.js's caching layers and why do they cause stale data surprises?
followUps.Time-based and on-demand revalidation co: How do time-based and on-demand revalidation differ?

evidence.text: Request memoization dedupes identical fetches within one render.
The Data Cache stores fetch results across requests and the Full Route Cache stores rendered pages.
The client Router Cache keeps visited pages in the browser, so a change may need invalidation in more than one layer.
A revalidate time refreshes cached data after a set number of seconds.
revalidatePath or revalidateTag clears the cache immediately when data changes.
Use on-demand after known edits and time-based for data that changes on its own.

groups.title: Data Fetching Patterns
groups.question: Your dashboard page loads user, orders and stats one after another and takes three seconds, and one widget needs live client-side data. Explain how you would fetch data.

followUps.fetch in Server Components with caching: How do fetch options control caching in a server component?
followUps.Parallel data fetching with Promise.all: Why use Promise.all for independent requests?
followUps.use client directive and client-side fet: When would you fetch in a client component, and with what?

evidence.text: Server components fetch data directly without an API layer.
Options choose whether the result is cached or fetched fresh.
A revalidate time keeps cached data reasonably fresh.
Awaiting requests one after another adds their times together.
Starting them together with Promise.all runs them at the same time.
Total time becomes that of the slowest request.
use client marks a component to run in the browser.
Client fetching suits data that changes with user interaction or must update live.
TanStack Query handles caching, refetching and loading states there.

groups.title: Suspense and Skeleton UI
groups.question: Your whole dashboard is blank until the slowest query finishes, and one failing widget breaks the entire page. Explain how Suspense and error boundaries fix this.

followUps.Suspense boundaries for incremental page: How does wrapping a slow component in Suspense help?
followUps.Error boundaries to gracefully handle fe: How does error.tsx stop one failure from breaking the whole page?

evidence.text: Suspense shows a fallback, like a skeleton, while the component loads.
The rest of the page renders immediately.
Content appears progressively instead of all at once.
error.tsx creates an error boundary for its segment.
A thrown error shows a fallback UI only for that segment.
The fallback can offer a reset to try again.
